atoms-blue.$description: Atoms Blue — Violet supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

atoms-blue-deep.$description: Atoms Blue Deep — Violet supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

mac-red.$description: Mac Red — Red supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis

mac-yellow.$description: Mac Yellow — Decorative window-chrome dot on template preview thumbnails

mac-green.$description: Mac Green — Decorative window-chrome dot on template preview thumbnails

canvas-mist.$description: Canvas Mist — Page-level background, hairline dividers, icon strokes — the dominant neutral that defines the system's floor

surface-white.$description: Surface White — Card backgrounds, input fields, elevated surfaces — the top layer of the surface stack

surface-fog.$description: Surface Fog — Subtle recessed surfaces, secondary card backgrounds, image overlays

ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Primary text, heading text, icon fills, input borders — near-black rather than pure black for less harshness

pure-black.$description: Pure Black — Maximum-contrast text, dark template preview surfaces, image elements requiring true black

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Secondary text, badge labels, muted icon fills — sits between Ink Black and the mid-grays

mid-gray.$description: Mid Gray — Tertiary text, placeholder text, disabled button labels, input helper text

silver.$description: Silver — Muted icon fills, decorative text, low-emphasis UI marks

border-gray.$description: Border Gray — Subtle borders and dividers where Canvas Mist feels too prominent

ibm-plex-sans.$description: The workhorse — body, buttons, nav, cards, badges, inputs, small headings. Plex Sans brings a technical, slightly geometric quality that reads as 'builder tool' rather than 'marketing page.' 400 for body, 500 for nav and button labels, 600 for card titles and section headings.

ibm-plex-serif.$description: The hero headline voice — used at 48px/600 exactly once on the page. A serif on a dev-tool site is anti-convention; it gives the main promise editorial weight while the rest of the UI stays in the sans-serif workshop tone. This single serif moment is the brand's typographic signature.
